David / team,

Thanks for the draft and the clear checklist. High-level reaction from Pinewave Legal / Ops: useful starting point, but several items will need hard language or alternative options. Attached is our short audit requirements exhibit (PW-Attachment-Audit-Reqs.pdf).

Main legal positions we will redline:
1) License scope: we cannot accept any language that implies unlimited copy or distribution of the runtime binary outside the on-prem environment. We will propose a narrower "sitting instance" license with strict locality and no external distribution rights.
2) Escrow / snapshot: Pinewave prefers a witness-based forensic snapshot approach rather than a deposit/escrow of binaries. We'll propose witnessless transfer only for catastrophic recovery with an additional tamper-evident manifest.
3) Access & credentials: Operator access must be limited to named individuals and require a Pinewave sponsor present for any elevated activity. Temporary access tokens must be issued by Pinewave KMS.
4) Audit window: 72 hours notice is more realistic for our internal compliance; we can be flexible for critical events.

On the technical front, Emma confirms Pinewave KMS supports HSM wrapping but the PKI cert rotation process requires a two-week lead for on-site key ceremonies.

I'll circulate annotated redlines by Friday EOD. A couple of items you'll likely flag as material: the license locality carveouts and an evidence-retention cap (we'll propose 45 days instead of 90). If we can't agree on retention, Pinewave will ask for a limited on-prem witness with a scrubbed-forensics workflow.

Best,
Alex Wang
Senior Counsel, Pinewave Therapeutics
alex.wang@pinewave.com
Attachment: PW-Attachment-Audit-Reqs.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Private installation annex — draft redline & evidence checklist

Grace / team — attached is a 1-page legal position and our proposed redline (RN-Grace-Pinewave-Annex-redline.docx). Summary below for quick consumption.

Summary (legal):
- Acceptable: witness-based forensic snapshots for diagnostics; Pinewave must agree to a limited scope and a certified chain-of-custody during sessions.
- Counter-proposal: retain our proposed 90-day diagnostic snapshot window but include a clause allowing Pinewave to request a curated, scrubbed report within 45 days for privacy reasons. This preserves our support diagnostics while giving Pinewave a path for privacy.
- License: proposed language that restricts binaries to the installation environment but permits patching and emergency hotfixes via secure agent with Pinewave logging. We add an audit trail requirement.
- Escrow-lite: propose an escrow-lite exhibit (internal) that allows for a sealed snapshot deposit accessible only under multi-party retrieval (Redwood ops + Pinewave Legal + neutral third-party auditor) — provides recovery without full public deposit.

Risk note: the two main negotiation points are (1) the retention cap, which affects our ability to debug regressions and (2) PKI ceremony lead times, which could delay deployment by up to three weeks if not accelerated. If Pinewave holds firm at 45 days and two-week key rotations, expect +$10k professional services to support on-site witness windows.

Next steps:
- I'll send the annotated redline directly to Alex tomorrow morning and request a short call to align on escrow-lite mechanics.
- David / Neha: please confirm whether the PS uplift of ~$10k is acceptable to the deal economics.

Attachments: RN-Grace-Pinewave-Annex-redline.docx (docx)

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
